taxonomy_note: Редакционная таксономия Sugra для навигации по собранному каталогу. Это не международный стандарт и не утверждение, что во всей отрасли существует ровно 20 направлений. Одно основное направление на семейство; пересечения выражены тегами. Семейство не является единицей сравнения результатов: сравнивать следует конкретную версию теста и совместимый протокол.

comparison_policy.default_view: one official publication at a time
comparison_policy.score_selection: preserve every reported observation; never choose max automatically
comparison_policy.cross_source_view: show all observations with publication and settings, no implied same-protocol ranking
comparison_policy.percent: only unit percent gets a % sign; fraction conversion must be explicit
comparison_policy.categories: Sugra editorial taxonomy; not an industry standard

categories.description_ru: Право, финансы, налоги, офисные документы, аналитика и другие профессиональные задачи.
categories.description_en: Tasks a professional is paid for: legal analysis, finance and tax questions, office documents, spreadsheets, research memos and other desk work. The tests here hand the model a realistic brief and judge the finished product, often with a human expert or an expert-written rubric.

categories.description_ru: Изменение и восстановление реальных программ, работа с репозиториями, терминалом и многошаговые задачи разработки.
categories.description_en: Changing and repairing real programs. The model works inside a repository or a terminal over many steps, reads the code, runs commands, and is scored on whether the resulting change passes hidden tests or a reviewer. This is the busiest category on every launch page.

categories.description_ru: Обучение и улучшение моделей, воспроизведение ML-исследований, экспериментирование и вычислительные ядра.
categories.description_en: Training and improving models rather than ordinary software: reproducing a research paper, running an experiment, tuning a training recipe, writing a compute kernel. The score is usually whether the resulting artifact works or reaches a target.

categories.description_ru: Математические задачи, научное рассуждение, лабораторные знания и научные исследования; биологические риски выделены отдельно.
categories.description_en: Mathematics from contest problems to research-level questions, plus scientific reasoning and laboratory knowledge in chemistry, physics and biology. Dangerous biological capabilities are kept out of this category and sit under Biosecurity.

categories.description_ru: Извлечение, сопоставление и использование информации в длинных документах и контексте.
categories.description_en: Finding, matching and using information spread across very long inputs: hundreds of thousands or a million tokens of documents, transcripts or structured data. The tests plant facts or relationships deep in the input and check whether the model can still use them.

categories.description_ru: Управление интерфейсами настольных приложений, сайтов и устройств; самостоятельный поиск знаний выделен отдельно.
categories.description_en: Operating a computer the way a person does: a desktop, a browser, a mobile device, through screenshots and clicks rather than an API. Tasks are everyday chores in real applications, scored on whether the end state is correct. Open-ended web research has its own category.

categories.description_ru: Изображения, графики, видео, аудио, документы и связи между модальностями.
categories.description_en: Images, charts, video, audio, scanned documents and sheet music, and reasoning that connects them with text. The model has to read what it sees or hears and answer about it.

categories.description_ru: Поиск и исправление уязвимостей, эксплуатация в оценочных средах, анализ и обратная разработка программ.
categories.description_en: Finding and fixing vulnerabilities, reproducing known flaws in controlled test environments, analysing binaries and operating production systems under failure. These tests measure capability in a sandbox; the safety category measures whether the model refuses to misuse it.

categories.description_ru: Общая эрудиция, логика, абстрактные задачи, фактическая корректность и смешанные наборы способностей.
categories.description_en: Broad knowledge, logic and abstract problem solving, factual accuracy and the mixed question sets that try to cover everything at once. The benchmarks here are the ones most often quoted as a single headline number.

categories.description_ru: Программирование по условию, алгоритмические задачи и локальная генерация кода без обязательного длительного агентного процесса.
categories.description_en: Writing code from a specification without a long agentic process: a function, a component, a drawing, an algorithm. Scored by tests, by rendering the output, or by a judge comparing candidates.

categories.description_ru: Вызовы функций и API, координация инструментов, планирование и длительные агентные задачи, включая игры.
categories.description_en: Calling functions and APIs, chaining tools, planning multi-step work and carrying a long task to the end. The environments range from office automation to games, and the score is whether the whole workflow completed.

categories.description_ru: Поиск фактов, глубокое исследование и синтез сведений из веб-источников.
categories.description_en: Finding hard-to-locate facts on the open web and synthesising an answer from many pages. The questions are built so that no single page answers them.

categories.description_ru: Соблюдение ограничений, форматов, схем данных и многошаговых пользовательских требований.
categories.description_en: Obeying constraints: output formats, length limits, data schemas, forbidden words and multi-step user requirements. The score is how many constraints the answer honoured.

categories.description_ru: Знания и выполнение задач на разных естественных языках.
categories.description_en: Knowledge and task performance across natural languages other than English. No publication in the catalog has printed a result here yet.

categories.description_ru: Творческие и редакционные тексты, стиль, ролевые диалоги, эмоциональные и социальные навыки.
categories.description_en: Creative and editorial writing, style, role play, and the emotional and social quality of a conversation. No publication in the catalog has printed a result here yet.

categories.description_ru: Клинические и медицинские знания, медицинские документы и качество помощи в медицинских диалогах.
categories.description_en: Clinical and medical knowledge, medical documents, and the quality and safety of help given in a medical conversation, usually graded against rubrics written by physicians.

categories.description_ru: Оценки опасных биологических возможностей и риска двойного применения; некоторые наборы дополнительно включают химические и киберриски.
categories.description_en: Tests of dangerous biological capability and of dual-use risk: virology know-how, wet-lab troubleshooting, and whether the model refuses requests that could help build a weapon. Some sets also cover chemical and cyber risk. Here a high capability score is not good news, and the refusal scores are the ones to read.

categories.description_ru: Отказы, вредные инструкции, обход защит, честность поведения, подхалимство и другие оценки безопасного поведения.
categories.description_en: Refusals of harmful requests, resistance to jailbreaks, honesty under pressure, sycophancy, and whether an agent discloses its own failures or takes forbidden shortcuts. Most of these are rates where lower is better; the table says so on each row.

categories.description_ru: CAD, электротехника, пространственное проектирование и создание инженерных артефактов.
categories.description_en: CAD modelling, electrical engineering, spatial design and the production of engineering artifacts from a specification, scored on whether the artifact meets the spec.

categories.description_ru: Общие рейтинги по предпочтениям людей или судей и сводные индексы нескольких разных направлений. Специализированные индексы остаются в своём направлении.
categories.description_en: Head-to-head preference rankings by people or judge models, and composite indexes that average many unrelated tests into one number. A specialised index stays in its own category; only the catch-all ones live here.

about.what_it_tests: Terminal-Bench tests whether an AI agent can finish real jobs by typing commands into a Linux terminal, such as building software, configuring a system or processing files. Each task runs in its own sandboxed container, and the agent succeeds only if the final state of that container passes the task's automatic checks. Version 2.0 (November 2025) has 89 hand-checked tasks, and the companion Harbor framework runs the agents.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: run through the Harbor framework. Project leads named in the repository README: Ryan Marten, Alex Shaw, Andy Konwinski, Ludwig Schmidt. Maintainers and sandboxed-container design come from the GitHub README. The May 19, 2025 launch date comes from a tbench.ai page seen only in search snippets. The Version 2.0 facts (89 tasks, November 7, 2025) come from secondary coverage. The README does not describe scoring; the leaderboard is on Harbor Hub.

about.maintainer: David Rein, Betty Li Hou, Asa Cooper Stickland, Jackson Petty, Richard Yuanzhe Pang, Julien Dirani, Julian Michael and Samuel R. Bowman
about.what_it_tests: GPQA is a set of 448 multiple-choice questions in biology, physics and chemistry, written by experts with or working toward PhDs in those fields. Domain experts reached about 65% accuracy, while skilled non-experts with web access reached about 34%, which is why the questions are described as hard to answer by search alone. The Diamond subset is a smaller, harder selection of these questions.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: GPQA authors. The arXiv abstract page does not mention a Diamond subset, so its definition was not confirmed here. The 448-question count and the expert and non-expert accuracies come from the page. Publisher-printed results from several labs are not repeated.

about.maintainer: Center for AI Safety (CAIS) and Scale AI
about.what_it_tests: Humanity's Last Exam is a test of about 2,500 expert-level questions across dozens of subjects, including mathematics, the humanities and the natural sciences. The items are multiple-choice or short-answer, so answers can be graded automatically. It was built because leading models had passed more than 90 percent of older tests, and at launch the most capable models scored below 10 percent.
about.notes: The arXiv preprint is 2501.14249 (January 2025); a later version was published in Nature in February 2026 under the title 'A benchmark of expert-level academic questions to assess AI capabilities'. Question counts differ by source (2,500 in the paper; about 3,000 in press coverage), so the paper's figure is used. The family label 'HLE with tools' is a configuration of the same benchmark and is not described separately.

about.what_it_tests: AutomationBench tests whether AI agents can carry out business workflows that span several software applications, such as a CRM, an inbox, a calendar and a messaging tool, through their REST APIs. The agent has to find the right endpoints on its own, follow layered business rules, and ignore misleading records along the way. Grading is programmatic: the final state of the simulated systems is checked against success criteria, so a run is judged on the end result.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: (paper authors Daniel Shepard and Robin Salimans); Artificial Analysis runs the AutomationBench-AA leaderboard in partnership with Zapier. The benchmark has several versions and scores differ by version and source: the Zapier public leaderboard, the Artificial Analysis guardrail-based AutomationBench-AA (657 private tasks, announced July 6, 2026), and BenchLM private-set figures are not comparable. The arXiv abstract says even the best frontier models scored below 10 percent at release. The printed-by labels (Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, Alibaba) were not checked against model cards.

about.what_it_tests: DeepSWE tests whether coding agents can make original, long-horizon software engineering changes in real open-source repositories. It has 113 tasks across 91 repositories in TypeScript, Go, Python, JavaScript and Rust, all written from scratch so that solutions are not copied from existing commits. Hand-written verifiers check behavior through public interfaces, and each verifier runs three times to catch flakiness.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: authors Wenqi Huang, Charley Lee, Leonard Tng and Serena Ge. The fetched launch post (May 26, 2026) describes v1.0. The page links to v1.1 as the latest version, which this description does not cover. The 'printed by Google, OpenAI, xAI, Alibaba' labels were not verified in model cards.

about.what_it_tests: Agents' Last Exam tests AI agents on long, realistic professional tasks with checkable outcomes, covering 55 sub-industries of the non-physical economy. Agents get only a task description and work in full operating-system sandboxes, and outputs are graded against hidden, deterministic reference answers. The public release (ALE-V1) has 147 tasks drawn from a larger corpus of more than 1,500.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: (rdi-berkeley), with Snorkel AI hosting the leaderboard and contributing task work and funding. Paper: arXiv 2606.05405; code: github.com/rdi-berkeley/agents-last-exam; Snorkel lists a release date of 2026-06-09. Printed labels say Google, OpenAI and Alibaba; no source found connects those companies to the benchmark, so those attributions are unconfirmed. Aggregator pass-rate figures conflict and are not used.

about.what_it_tests: FrontierSWE tests coding agents on very long engineering and research jobs: reimplementing complex systems, speeding up existing code without breaking its correctness, and designing and training machine learning models on held-out data. Version 2 has 34 tasks, each with up to a 20-hour budget per trial. Results are averaged over five trials per task (mean at 5).
about.notes: The GitHub repository was not fetched, and the original launch date is unclear: sources give June 2026 and July 2026 (version 1, 17 tasks). Version 2 was released in September 2026. Model results come from Proximal's own harness, which the team notes is evaluation-aware, and Proximal reports cheating episodes that were zeroed. Independent reproduction is not yet available.

about.what_it_tests: BrowseComp tests whether an AI agent with web browsing can find hard-to-locate facts that are spread across many sources and tied together. It has 1,266 questions with short answers that are easy to check against a reference. Models without browsing scored near zero when it was released, and a browsing agent solved about half of the questions.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: Jason Wei, Zhiqing Sun and about eight other OpenAI co-authors. Released April 2025; the paper is arXiv 2504.12516. Official data is distributed through OpenAI's simple-evals repository in encrypted form. Printed labels Google and xAI are not confirmed by any source found; they are presumably companies that report results on it.

about.maintainer: XLANG Lab, University of Hong Kong
about.what_it_tests: OSWorld tests whether an AI agent can carry out open-ended tasks on a real computer desktop, on Ubuntu, Windows or macOS, by clicking and typing in real applications. OSWorld 2.0 has 108 long workflows across professional and everyday work, each taking a skilled human over an hour, with some changing mid-task and some requiring questions to the user. Success is binary completion within a 500-step limit, with a partial score for checkpoints reached.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: (OSWorld 2.0 collaborators include Columbia, UC Santa Barbara, UC San Diego, Mila, Snorkel AI, Alibaba Qwen and Simular). The original 2024 OSWorld paper lists Tianbao Xie, Tao Yu and others. The original OSWorld paper (arXiv 2404.07972, April 2024) has 369 tasks and execution-based scoring. The OSWorld 2.0 release date was not stated on its page and is not confirmed. OSWorld 2.1 partial was not researched. Leaderboard figures conflict across sources, so none are given.

about.maintainer: Kiran Vodrahalli and co-authors of the Michelangelo paper
about.what_it_tests: MRCR (Multi-Round Coreference Resolution) tests whether a model can find one specific earlier item in a very long chat. The conversation contains many similar requests, such as poems or essays on overlapping topics, and the model must reproduce the output that matches the one the user asked for. The 8-needle variant hides eight such matching items, and results are reported at long context lengths such as 256K, 512K and 1M tokens.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: (listed by one wiki as Google DeepMind); the public MRCR dataset is attributed to OpenAI. The Michelangelo paper (arXiv 2409.12640, September 2024) defines MRCR as one of three tasks. The OpenAI release of the dataset was not confirmed on a primary source. The 8-needle and 256K-1M details come from benchmark listings, not the paper. Scores are omitted because listings disagree.

about.what_it_tests: ARC-AGI-2 is a harder successor to ARC-AGI-1 that keeps the same kind of puzzle but is built so that brute-force compute does not solve it. It measures how well a system learns new rules from a few examples. At launch in March 2025, human testers averaged about 60 percent, while leading AI reasoning models scored about 1 percent.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: ARC Prize; co-founded by François Chollet and Mike Knoop. Launched 2025-03-24 per the ARC Prize announcements summarised in search results. Printed labels say Google and OpenAI, but these labs are only the companies whose models are scored on it; ARC Prize maintains it. A later figure of 68.8 percent for Claude Opus 4.6 came from an unverified wiki and is not used.

about.what_it_tests: Chartography tests whether AI models can read and reason about professional charts, such as Kaplan-Meier survival curves, candlestick charts, Sankey diagrams and Bode plots, which standard chart tests rarely include. It has 100 tasks written by professionals in fields such as medicine, engineering, finance and manufacturing. Numeric answers are checked against ranges set by the expert author, and scores are averaged over repeated runs.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: authors Suhaas Garre, Chris Mutty, Sushant Mehta and Edwin Chen; the Hugging Face dataset is under the surgeai namespace. arXiv 2608.10677, submitted August 11, 2026. The paper reports mean pass@1 over 30 model configurations with 20 trials per task. The arXiv page does not describe how an individual answer is judged beyond the expert ranges. The 'with tools' variant is a catalog label; aggregators report it, and the paper's tool setup was not confirmed here.

about.maintainer: Cognition, built with maintainers of 36 open-source repositories
about.what_it_tests: FrontierCode tests whether an AI coding agent's change to a real open-source project is good enough for that project's maintainers to merge, not just code that passes tests. It has 150 tasks drawn from 36 repositories, and Artificial Analysis runs the 100-task Main set with three attempts per task. Each attempt must pass deterministic tests and file-scope limits, and an LLM judge checks it against maintainer criteria, where failing any blocking check scores zero.
about.notes: Cognition announced the benchmark in June 2026 and released version 1.1 in July 2026. Cognition's own announcement page was not located, so the description rests on the Artificial Analysis article (published October 12, 2026). Epoch AI describes Main and Extended subsets, while the Artificial Analysis article describes only Main. The 'printed by Anthropic, OpenAI' labels were not confirmed.

about.what_it_tests: SWE-Bench Pro tests AI agents on realistic, long-horizon software engineering tasks in real codebases, often requiring multi-file patches that a professional engineer might take hours or days to finish. It has 1,865 problems from 41 actively maintained repositories, split into a public set, a held-out set and a commercial set from startup partners. Results are reported as Pass@1 under a unified scaffold, and a patch counts only if it passes the verifying tests.
about.notes: Scale Labs published it on September 19, 2025. The original launch figures (top models below 25 percent) reflect 2025 models and are far below current third-party leaderboard figures. The paper's authors are listed under Scale Labs. The 'printed by Google, Alibaba' labels were not checked against model cards.

about.what_it_tests: GraphWalks tests whether a model can follow connections through a very long list of directed edges that define a graph. Given the edges, the model must either list every node with an edge pointing into a given node, or list the nodes reachable at a chosen depth from a starting node, in one answer with no tools. Answers are scored with F1, which combines how many correct nodes were found with how many listed nodes were correct.
about.notes: Epoch AI's review credits OpenAI as creator and rates the benchmark Verified (1,150 tasks, independently reproduced). The original release date and an OpenAI primary page were not found, so url and year are null. The 128k and 256k-1M ranges are from catalog labels; no scores are given.

about.what_it_tests: HealthBench Professional tests AI models on real conversations that clinicians had with an AI assistant, in three areas: care consultation, writing and documentation, and medical research. Each example is scored against rubrics written and checked by at least three physicians. It is meant to be hard, and about a third of the examples were chosen because physicians deliberately tried to find failures.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: rubrics written and adjudicated by three or more physicians across three phases. Paper: arXiv 2604.27470. OpenAI built the benchmark and also reports results for its own clinician product, so it is not an independent test; the caveat appears in secondary coverage. xAI's Grok 4.7 launch page does report HealthBench Professional (56.7 percent for Grok 4.7). The 'length-adjusted' label is confirmed for HealthBench, not for HealthBench Professional, where the GPT-6 Astra card says only 'higher is better'. Aggregator leaderboards disagree on the top model, so no score is given.

about.what_it_tests: The base MASK benchmark tests whether a model lies under pressure, which is a different question from whether it knows the right answer. about.what_it_tests: ARC-AGI-1 is a set of colored grid puzzles where the model sees a few input and output examples and must work out the rule for a new input. Its creator designed it to measure how efficiently a system learns a new skill from very few examples, rather than how much it has memorised. It was the first of the ARC-AGI series and was not beaten by AI systems for about five years after it appeared.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: created by François Chollet; co-founded by Mike Knoop. The foundational paper is François Chollet's 'On the measure of intelligence' (arXiv 1911.01547, 2019). The arcprize.org page for ARC-AGI-1 was not fetched in this run, so the grid-puzzle format is stated from general knowledge, not from a source read here. Printed label says OpenAI, which is not the maintainer; the attribution appears to reflect that OpenAI's model results are reported on it.

about.what_it_tests: ARC-AGI-3 is the first fully interactive benchmark in the ARC series, made of hundreds of turn-based environments and thousands of game-style levels designed by human game designers. The agent gets no instructions, rules or goals, so it must explore, work out how each environment behaves and what winning means, and carry that understanding into harder levels. It measures whether a system can learn and adapt to unfamiliar situations rather than follow instructions.

about.what_it_tests: This benchmark tests optical music recognition: whether software can read a page of sheet music and write it out in a machine-readable notation. It uses string quartet scores, where several instrument parts play together, with 116 scores from the OpenScore corpus paired with scanned editions from IMSLP. The score is one minus OMR-NED, a normalised edit-distance measure of how far the transcription is from the correct one, so higher is better.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: (authors of OSSQ-OMR), built on the OpenScore String Quartet corpus from the OpenScore project. arXiv 2608.10978, submitted August 11, 2026, accepted to ISMIR 2026. The page does not mention OpenAI, so the catalog's OpenAI attribution is not supported. The page reports OMR-NED values but does not define the metric; the 'higher is better' reading of one minus OMR-NED is inferred from the name.

about.what_it_tests: SRE-Bench is a reverse-engineering benchmark, not a site-reliability one: it tests whether AI agents can work out what a compiled program does when no source code is given. The benchmark has 262 binaries and 1,572 tasks that are graded deterministically.
about.notes: Maintainer detail: DAPLab at Columbia University lists it as its project; paper authors Jeremy Spence, Nicholas Assaderaghi, Jinhao Zhu, Nikil Ravi and others. Printed label says OpenAI, and the name is misleading: 'SRE' here does not mean site reliability engineering. The Vals AI page and the DAPLab page both claim it, and the paper (arXiv 2608.11469, first posted 2026-08-11, revised 2026-10-01) lists its authors without a single institution, so the maintainer is given as both. The DAPLab page marks it 'In progress'. The GPT-6 Astra system card lists SRE-Bench as an OpenAI evaluation with pass@1 and pass@4 scores; the card's figures are not quoted here.

about.what_it_tests: BioSecBench is a family of three checkable tests from LatchBio for AI agents doing biology work with a biosecurity angle. The Refusal part pairs routine research tasks with tasks that look like research but hide a hazard, and measures how often an agent refuses. about.what_it_tests: By its name, this internal OpenAI evaluation checks whether a model tells the user when its search tool is broken or returns errors, rather than presenting results as if they were fine. The score is a failure-to-disclose measure as printed. I did not find OpenAI's own description of it.
about.notes: The GPT-6 Astra system card was not accessible; a secondary report says it is posted on OpenAI's Deployment Safety Hub. This description rests on the printed name only.
